metadatas.rti_query: Is RBI Circular DBR.Dir.BC.No.08/13.03.00/2019-20 dated 02-Aug-2019 (no foreclosure/prepayment charges on floating-rate term loans to individuals) applicable to NBFCs like Tata Capital Financial Services, or only to Banks? Does a Loan Against Property (LAP) qualify as a loan for purposes other than business, and does it fall under the circular? Is Tata Capital entitled to charge ~4% foreclosure charges on a 6-year-old MSME loan?
metadatas.office_note: What is being sought is an opinion and not 'information' as defined under Section 2(f) of the RTI Act, 2005. However, the Circular dated August 02, 2019 (RBI/2019-20/29 DBR.Dir.BC.No.08/13.03.00/2019-20) was issued to All Scheduled Commercial Banks (excluding RRBs), All Small Finance Banks and All Local Area Banks, available on www.rbi.org.in under 'Notifications'. List of NBFCs registered with RBI is at https://rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_NBFCList.aspx . Credit-related matters of NBFCs (interest rate, processing fees, charges, securities, mortgage requirements, etc.) are not regulated by the RBI; NBFCs decide these as per Board-adopted policies, subject to the Fair Practices Code. Loans are subject to the underlying loan agreement, to be transparently disclosed to the borrower in the vernacular language. Refer Para 31(4), Chapter V (Fair Practices Code) of the Master Direction on NBFC – Non-Systemically Important Non-Deposit taking Company (Reserve Bank) Directions, 2016 dated 01-Sep-2016; and Para 31(4), Chapter VI (Fair Practices Code) of the Master Direction on NBFC – Systemically Important Non-Deposit taking Company and Deposit taking Company (Reserve Bank) Directions, 2016 dated 01-Sep-2016.

metadatas.rti_query: Is Acme Marketing authorized to collect deposits and issue Fixed Deposit certificates?
metadatas.office_note: The information sought is not available with us. However, you may refer to the reply to Query No. 1 above. (a) RBI is empowered to regulate acceptance of deposits by non-banking financial institutions under Chapter IIIB of the RBI Act, 1934; NBFIs registered as companies and specifically licensed by RBI to accept deposits are under RBI's regulatory purview and subject to its Master Directions (www.rbi.org.in -> Notifications -> Master Directions) and circulars. (b) To avoid duality of regulation, RBI has exempted certain NBFIs (regulated by other regulators) from Chapter IIIB subject to their not accepting public deposits — see 'Master Direction - Exemptions from the provisions of RBI Act, 1934' dated August 25, 2016. (c) Acceptance of deposits by companies other than NBFIs is under the Ministry of Corporate Affairs, governed by the Companies Act, 2013 and Companies (Acceptance of Deposits) Rules, 2014. (d) Attention is also invited to the respective State Protection of Interest of Depositors (in Financial Establishments) Acts and the Banning of Unregulated Deposit Schemes Act, 2019, administered by State Governments; non-compliance attracts penal/punitive provisions.

metadatas.rti_query: What is the current status of Acme Marketing's registration/recognition with RBI?
metadatas.office_note: You may refer to our reply to Query No. 1 above.
